fullPassage:
Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students.

This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services.

Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to afford the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true win-win situation.

Hi! My name is Jacob Jansen, and I've been living at Humanitas for over two years. As a live-in student, I'm required to spend at least 30 hours per month with my elderly neighbors in exchange for free accommodations. In reality, however, we spend a lot more time together than that. Sometimes I teach them things, such as how to use social media, and other times I just hang out with them. We have meals together, play games, and go shopping.

Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home to me. Instead, I consider it a community that I am a part of. Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to acquire. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them.

I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do. Obviously, Humanitas provides me with much more than a free place to stay. I've made deep, meaningful friendships that I'll never forget here.

I intend to stay at Humanitas for at least one more year. Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this transformative experience.

My name is Helena Smit, and I am 93 years old. I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. Believe me, not everyone was happy about it! But that quickly changed once they moved in. The students here are energetic, friendly, and caring. They make us laugh and create a joyful mood.

Humanitas was already a decent place to live before the students arrived, but it has become a lot more fun since they moved in. Recently, the students held a pajama party and invited us to join them. It was like we were in our 20s again.

I sometimes hear loud music from my young next-door neighbor's apartment, but that is okay. It's a small matter compared to what they've brought to our lives.

She went through a difficult time of grief after she lost her father. I stayed with her, held her hands when she cried, and listened to what she said. She later told me that I was a great comfort during that difficult time.

I am nearly 100 years old, and I have bad knees. But having young, vibrant people around helps me forget about the pain and enjoy my life!

There are currently six students living at Humanitas, with a long waiting list. Humanitas is a great example of how people of different ages can help each other. The older residents gain a more youthful perspective on life, while the younger residents receive valuable life lessons. More and more care homes around Europe are now trying intergenerational living, bringing the young and old together in harmony.

questions.passage: Hi! My name is Jacob Jansen, and I've been living at Humanitas for over two years. As a live-in student, I'm required ①<u>spend</u> at least 30 hours per month with my elderly neighbors in exchange for free accommodations. In reality, however, we spend a lot more time together than that. Sometimes I teach them things, such as how to use social media, and other times I just ②<u>hang</u> out with them. We have meals together, play games, and go ③<u>shopping</u>. Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home ④<u>to</u> me.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문은 'I'm required to spend'인데, to가 빠져서 틀림. be required to + 동사원형 구문.
det.analysis:
❌ ① spend → to spend: be required to V(~하도록 요구되다). to부정사 필요
✅ ② hang: I just hang out — 동사원형 정상
✅ ③ shopping: go shopping — go + V-ing 정상
✅ ④ to: feel like ~ to me — 전치사 to 정상
det.tip: be required to V = ~하도록 요구되다. require + O + to V의 수동태. to 누락 주의.

questions.passage: Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center ①<u>that</u> houses more than 160 elderly residents ②<u>who</u> require assistance. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 주어 residents(복수)이므로 동사는 share. shares → share.
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: 관계대명사 that, 선행사 center 수식 정상
✅ ② who: 관계대명사 who, 선행사 residents(사람) 수식 정상
✅ ③ offers: 주어 Humanitas(단수) + offers 정상
❌ ④ shares → share: 주어 residents(복수)이므로 share 필요
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: 복수 주어(residents) + 복수 동사(share). 단수 shares는 불가.

questions.passage: Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms ①<u>available</u>, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for ②<u>spend</u> time with the elderly residents. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'in return for spending'인데, 전치사 for 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 필요. spend → spending.
det.analysis:
✅ ① available: 형용사 후치수식(rooms available) 정상
❌ ② spend → spending: 전치사 for + 동명사(-ing) 필요
✅ ③ struggling: were struggling — 과거진행형 정상
✅ ④ win-win: 복합형용사 정상
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사: in return for spending = ~하는 대가로. for 뒤에 동사원형 불가.

questions.passage: With so much experience ①<u>gathered</u> over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to ②<u>acquire</u>. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without ③<u>realizing</u> it. I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I ④<u>focusing</u> only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'I focused only on'인데, focusing으로 바뀌어 틀림. 주어+동사 구조에서 과거형 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① gathered: 과거분사가 experience를 수식(경험이 모아진) 정상
✅ ② acquire: have yet to + 동사원형 정상
✅ ③ realizing: without + 동명사 정상
❌ ④ focusing → focused: because절의 술어동사 자리. 과거형 focused 필요
det.tip: because I focused: 접속사 because 뒤 주어+동사 구조. 동명사 focusing은 술어동사 불가.

questions.passage: This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts ①<u>reduced</u> the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the ②<u>loss</u> of many essential elderly care programs. Humanitas needed to seek an ③<u>expensive</u> solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free ④<u>accommodations</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 예산 삭감 후 '저렴한' 해결책을 찾아야 했으므로 expensive(비싼) → affordable(저렴한)이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reduced(줄였다): budget cuts reduced — 원문 그대로
✅ ② loss(상실): led to the loss — 원문 그대로
❌ ③ expensive(비싼) → affordable(저렴한): 예산 삭감 상황에서 비싼 해결책은 모순
✅ ④ accommodations(숙소): free accommodations — 원문 그대로
det.tip: affordable(감당할 수 있는, 저렴한) ↔ expensive(비싼). 예산 삭감 맥락 = 저렴한 해결책 필요.

questions.passage: I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. They make us laugh and create a ③<u>joyful</u> mood. Humanitas was already a decent place to live before the students arrived, but it has become a lot more ④<u>boring</u> since they moved in.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 학생들이 이사 온 후 더 '재미있게' 됐다는 문맥. boring(지루한) → fun(재미있는)이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① happy(행복한): not everyone was happy — 원문 그대로
✅ ② energetic(활기찬): 원문 그대로
✅ ③ joyful(즐거운): joyful mood — 원문 그대로
❌ ④ boring(지루한) → fun(재미있는): 학생들이 파자마 파티를 열고 초대하는 등 긍정적 변화 문맥
det.tip: fun(재미있는) ↔ boring(지루한). 학생들이 온 후 긍정적 변화를 강조하는 맥락.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 노인은 도움을 받고, 학생은 무료 숙소를 얻으니 윈윈(win-win situation).
det.analysis:
✅ ② win-win situation: 양쪽 모두 이득을 보는 상황. 원문 그대로
❌ ① financial burden(재정적 부담): 무료 숙소 제공이므로 부담이 아님
❌ ③ social experiment(사회적 실험): 실험이 아닌 실질적 해결책
❌ ④ temporary measure(임시 조치): 2012년부터 지속, 임시가 아님
det.tip: win-win situation = 양쪽 모두 이득인 상황. 학생(무료 숙소) + 노인(도움/교류).

questions.passage: Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. ch: how to manage my finances effectively

det.analysis:
✅ ③ the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee: 원문 그대로. 커피 한잔하며 가벼운 대화를 나누는 것의 가치
❌ ① 재정 관리: 언급 없음
❌ ② 학업 성취의 중요성: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 노인이 혼자 시간 보내기 선호: 함께 시간을 보내는 내용이므로 반대
det.tip: casual chat = 가벼운 대화. over a cup of coffee = 커피 한잔하며. 소소한 것의 가치를 배움.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 세대 간 공동생활 프로젝트는 2012년에 예산 삭감 이후 시작되었다.

det.korean: 원문: 'began in 2012, after budget cuts' = 예산 삭감 이후 2012년에 시작.

❌ ② 추가 예산 지원: 예산이 삭감됨(budget cuts)

det.tip: budget cuts = 예산 삭감. intergenerational living = 세대 간 공동생활.

det.korean: 원문: 'much more than a free place to stay' = 무료 숙소 이상의 것을 제공. '유일한 장점'이라는 것은 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 불일치: 무료 숙소 이상의 것(우정 등)을 제공받음. '유일한 장점'은 원문 반대
❌ ① 일치: 'I focused only on the things they can't do'
❌ ② 일치: 'deep, meaningful friendships'
❌ ③ 일치: 'intend to stay for at least one more year'
det.tip: much more than = ~보다 훨씬 많은. 무료 숙소는 여러 장점 중 하나일 뿐.

questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Humanitas의 관장은 지역 대학생들에게 무료 __________을/를 제공하기로 했다.". (1단어)

det.korean: 관장은 무료 숙소(accommodations)를 제공하기로 했다.
det.analysis: 원문 'decided to offer local university students free accommodations'에서 accommodations를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: accommodation(s) = 숙소, 숙박시설. free accommodations = 무료 숙소.

questions.passage: Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this (transform) experience. My name is Helena Smit, and I am 93 years old. I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors.
questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하시오.

(transform) → __________

det.korean: 이 변혁적인(transformative) 경험. 명사(experience)를 수식하는 형용사 필요.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

"Humanitas is a place where elderly residents and university students live together, providing (A)__________ benefits to both groups through (B)__________ interaction."

det.korean: (A) mutual(상호적인) + (B) intergenerational(세대 간) = 세대 간 교류를 통한 상호 이점.
det.analysis:
✅ ① mutual + intergenerational: 양쪽 모두 이득(mutual), 세대 간 교류(intergenerational)
❌ ② financial + professional: 재정적/전문적이 아닌 정서적 교류 중심
❌ ③ temporary + occasional: 지속적 프로젝트이며 일상적 교류
❌ ④ academic + institutional: 학문적/제도적 관계가 아닌 인간적 유대
det.tip: mutual = 상호적인. intergenerational = 세대 간. 이 두 단어가 글의 핵심 키워드.
